newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FRENCH TAX RISE COULD HIT QUICK - ANALYSTS.
newsitem.headline: FRENCH TAX RISE COULD HIT QUICK - ANALYSTS.

text.p: Shares in Belgian hamburger chain Quick fell sharply in Brussels on Thursday and dealers said they could sink further if France bowed to parliamentary pressure and raised value added tax (VAT) on fast food.
Quick was down 100 Belgian francs or 4.2 percent at 2,265 francs by late afternoon after a recent rally from lows reached on a profit warning petered out.

Dealers and analysts said Thursday's fall was not related to news the French parliament wants to raise VAT on fast food to 20.6 from 5.5 percent. But they said if the tax was confirmed in France's 1997 budget Quick's share could suffer further.
"It would be very disappointing. France is an important market for Quick," BBL analyst Ann Vanhelmont said.

Quick's share plunged to a low of 2,240 francs on September 23 on disappointment at first half 1996 earnings and a warning that full year profit could be 35 percent below 1995's 598 million francs. But the shares then staged a rally, reaching 2,450 on October 2.
"Fundamentally I think its right the share price is going down again," Vanhelmont said.
A trader at a Ghent-based brokerage said the share had risen purely due to retail interest.
"There were always big sellers about so now the retail interest has disappeared (Quick is) going back down," he said.
Quick is in the middle of a big investment programme to expand its French network. It opened 22 new outlets in the first half of 1996, 15 of which were in France.
It has said it wants to open a total of 60 new restaurants in 1996.
Shares in Belgian retailer GIB, which controls Quick, were down four francs at 1,294 francs.
